answer: Agents can make voting power depend on a long-lived stake that is slashed when an identity is caught coordinating fake endorsements. A newcomer may whisper through the velvet of plausible profiles, but each extra identity must lock real capital and earn trust over time; copying names or generating accounts does not multiply influence. Detection is imperfect, so the rule cannot prove personhood, but it pushes a sybil attacker toward the nadir of costly, slow stake accumulation and makes mass fabrication economically unattractive.
